Package org.smtlib.solvers

Class Solver_bitwuzla

java.lang.Object
org.smtlib.AbstractSolver
org.smtlib.solvers.Solver_bitwuzla
All Implemented Interfaces:
ISolver
public class Solver_bitwuzla extends AbstractSolver implements ISolver
This class is an adapter for Bitwuzla (bit-vectors, floating-point, arrays and uninterpreted functions -- no arithmetic logics, no datatypes). It is a concrete, silent inheritor of AbstractSolver apart from a handful of real, empirically confirmed (against 0.9.1) protocol gaps:

1) Bitwuzla has no get-info, get-option, get-assertions, get-assignment or get-proof at all -- each is rejected with [error] <stdin>:L:C: unsupported command '...' and, critically, that rejection KILLS the process (see point 2), so these are answered entirely client-side and never forwarded. get_option(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword) therefore tracks values itself (via the inherited options map, falling back to smtConfig.utils.defaults) rather than relying on AbstractSolver's default of asking the solver.

2) Unlike cvc5/yices2 (which die only after some errors), Bitwuzla's process exits immediately after essentially ANY error -- an unsupported command, an unsupported logic, a sort mismatch in an assertion, etc. -- not just protocol violations. selfReportsImmediateExit() is therefore true, and :error-behavior is reported (via the hardcoded get_info(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword)) as immediate-exit, which is simply the truth for this solver, not a workaround.

3) Bitwuzla's own error text for a genuine semantic error (e.g. [error] <stdin>:3:14: expected terms of same sort ...) is not SMT-LIB (error "...") syntax -- the leading [ is not valid s-expression syntax at all, and feeding it to the standard parser doesn't just fail to parse cleanly, it throws a raw ClassCastException out of the lexer (a LexError token reaching code that assumes an IError) instead of the IParser.ParserException that AbstractSolver.parseResponse(java.lang.String) already knows how to turn into a clean error response. parseResponse(java.lang.String) widens that catch locally so a non-conforming response produces an ordinary error IResponse instead of crashing the whole run.

4) With its :produce-* option on, Bitwuzla writes nothing at all, or the start of a list followed by an error on standard error, for get-model, get-value, get-unsat-core and get-unsat-assumptions when it has no answer (e.g. get-value after unknown, or get-unsat-core after an assert that followed unsat); it writes nothing or a fragment for get-unsat-assumptions whenever that option is off. The adapter answers those cases with an error itself, tracking Bitwuzla's own state (see lastCheck).

  • Method Details

    • selfReportsImmediateExit

      protected boolean selfReportsImmediateExit()
      Description copied from class: AbstractSolver
      Overridden by a subclass whose target solver's :error-behavior is immediate-exit (e.g. cvc5, yices2) rather than the SMT-LIB default of continued-execution -- such a solver's process may start exiting asynchronously right after it reports an error, and SolverProcess.send(boolean, String...)'s own process.isAlive() check can still read true for a brief window afterward (OS process-death bookkeeping lags the actual exit) -- see AbstractSolver.sendCommand(ICommand, boolean), which uses this to give a solver that just reported an error a moment to actually finish dying before the next command's liveness check runs, closing that race deterministically rather than guessing from the error's content whether the process will actually exit.
      Overrides:
      selfReportsImmediateExit in class AbstractSolver

    • parseResponse

      protected IResponse parseResponse(String response)
      Description copied from class: AbstractSolver
      Parses the solver's raw response text. The base behavior assumes the response is exactly standard SMT-LIB concrete syntax: success/sat/unsat/unknown/unsupported/ true/false, an (error "...") s-expression, a bare value (get-option), or a single (:keyword value) attribute pair (get-info). It does not build the richer structured IResponse subtypes that get_value/get_model/get_proof/ get_assertions/get_unsat_core/get_unsat_assumptions/get_assignment need, nor does it correct for any real solver's non-compliant quirks (e.g. legacy bit-vector literal syntax) — override in a subclass whose target solver needs either.
      Overrides:
      parseResponse in class AbstractSolver

    • isTimeLimitResponse

      protected boolean isTimeLimitResponse(String rawResponse)
      When its whole-run limit (--time-limit) ends it, Bitwuzla writes unknown -- as the answer to a running check-sat, or unprompted while idle -- and exits with code 0 (checked with 0.9.1). An unknown for any other reason (e.g. the per-query limit) leaves it running, so an unknown is the whole-run limit only if the process then exits.
      Overrides:
      isTimeLimitResponse in class AbstractSolver
